title: Holding Several Domain Registrations on One Account
content:
## Registration terms — number of holdings per account

**Clause 1.** A customer of Harborline Hosting & Domains may hold any number of Domain Registrations. Each domain name is a separate holding, and there is no per-customer cap on the number of holdings an account may carry.

**Clause 2.** A new registration or an inbound transfer of a domain name may be opened only when no other holding of the same domain name is in status pending, active, on hold, grace, redemption or pending delete.

**Clause 3.** A name whose earlier holding ended as deleted, transferred out or cancelled may be registered or transferred in again, and it is then opened as a new holding.

### Basis of the check

The check in Clause 2 rests on the system record: the statuses of the existing holdings that carry the same domain name, read before the new registration or inbound transfer is opened. The object compared is the domain name of the order, matched against the domain name on each existing holding. What the customer says about an earlier holding does not replace that record.

### Status of an existing holding of the same name — decision table

| Status of the other holding of the same name | New registration or inbound transfer of that name |
|---|---|
| pending | not opened |
| active | not opened |
| on hold | not opened |
| grace | not opened |
| redemption | not opened |
| pending delete | not opened |
| deleted | may be opened as a new holding |
| transferred out | may be opened as a new holding |
| cancelled | may be opened as a new holding |

### Points of judgement

- *Is there a limit on how many Domain Registrations one account holds?* No: the number of holdings is not capped per customer.
- *A name sits in redemption on the account. Can a fresh registration of the same name be opened?* No; a holding of that name in redemption is one of the statuses that keeps a second holding of the same name from being opened.
- *A name was transferred out to another registrar and the customer now brings it back.* The earlier holding ended as transferred out, so the inbound transfer is opened as a new holding.
